title.narrative: Save the Children support in South Sudan 2013-2014

description.narrative:
The project consisted of three overall components. 1) Phase II of the consolidated UN humanitarian response in Doro camp, Upper Nile where the project built on knowledge and experience gained while delivering an integrated package of Education in Emergencies, Child Protection in Emergencies, and psychosocial support to refugees in Doro Camp with support from UNHCR and DANIDA. Phase II of the Doro camp response scaled up the reach of existing programming, improving the access to inclusive education in a protective environment, and providing vulnerable children with appropriate community based child protection and psychosocial support services; 2) Improving the protection and psychosocial well-being of children affected by conflict in Jonglei State. Mobile Child Friendly Spaces¿ were established at IDP sites through emergency response programming, and where possible more permanent structures were established to offer children more structured and long-term support; 3) Support to the conflict response with plastic sheets, blankets, jerry cans and bladder tanks.
Due to the political conflict between Sudanese People¿s Liberation Army (SPLA) and the rebel groups, the project added the third component in order to target the conflict response in Juba. This was added after the initial concept note was approved. The project achieved the expected results, and SCD is awaiting final project report
